# Jay Patrick Cano (0xp47) — Portfolio

My personal developer portfolio built with Next.js (App Router), Tailwind CSS, and Framer Motion. It showcases my projects, work experience, and developer journey, optimized for clean performance and readability.

---

## 🚀 Key Features

* **Modular Architecture**: Clean separation of concerns with components structured by logical usage.
* **Search & AI Discoverability**:
  * **Structured Data**: JSON-LD Schema (`Person` entity) mapping aliases (`0xp47`), location details, and technical expertise.
  * **Crawler Friendly**: Configured `robots.txt` rules and automated dynamic `sitemap.xml` mapping.
  * **FAQ Structure**: Structured FAQ microdata compliant with schema formats to enhance readability for search engines and AI assistants.
* **Interactive Design**:
  * **Particle Background**: Code symbol background animations that dynamically connect on scroll.
  * **Cursor Aura**: Subtle glowing radial gradient tracking cursor movements.
  * **Smooth Scrolling**: Custom ease-in-out-cubic scroll animations for navigating anchor sections.
  * **Motion Reduction Support**: Respects system preferences (`prefers-reduced-motion`) to disable animations when requested.

---

## 🛠️ Technology Stack

* **Core**: Next.js 16 (App Router / Turbopack), React 19, TypeScript
* **Styling**: Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion (v12)
* **Icons**: Lucide React, Simple Icons (`react-icons/si`)
* **Fonts**: Geist Sans & Geist Mono (optimized local loading)

---

## 📁 Codebase Directory Structure

The components and hooks are organized using Next.js path aliases (`@/*`) to prevent relative directory path nesting:

```text
src/
├── app/                                # App Router Configurations
│   ├── favicon.ico
│   ├── globals.css                     # Custom Tailwind Theme Setup
│   ├── layout.tsx                      # Root Layout, Metadata & JSON-LD
│   ├── page.tsx                        # Home Route
│   ├── robots.ts                       # Robots.txt generator
│   └── sitemap.ts                      # Sitemap.xml generator
├── hooks/
│   └── use-safe-reduced-motion.ts      # Media query reduced-motion checker
├── components/
│   ├── layout/
│   │   ├── site-nav.tsx                # Page header sticky navigation
│   │   └── footer.tsx                  # Page copyright footer
│   ├── sections/
│   │   ├── hero-section.tsx            # Landing header & tech marquee loop
│   │   ├── about-section.tsx           # Bio highlights & animated counters
│   │   ├── services-section.tsx        # Services carousel & offerings
│   │   ├── projects-section.tsx        # Project catalog with category filtering
│   │   ├── blog-section.tsx            # Technical articles & blog cards
│   │   ├── experience-section.tsx      # Chronological history timeline
│   │   ├── certifications-section.tsx  # Cisco NetAcad & Credly verified badges
│   │   └── contact-section.tsx         # CTAs & email/social links
│   ├── shared/
│   │   ├── section.tsx                 # Shared viewport animate sections wrapper
│   │   ├── project-card.tsx            # Interactive project preview cards
│   │   ├── blog-card.tsx               # Blog post card component
│   │   └── particles-background.tsx    # Shared background code particle canvas
│   ├── portfolio.tsx                   # Main layout compositor
│   └── providers.tsx                   # Tooltip & global context providers
├── lib/
│   ├── portfolio-data.ts               # Local data model profiles & section meta
│   ├── certifications.json             # Cached Cisco NetAcad / Credly badges
│   ├── projects.json                   # Cached GitHub repositories & stats
│   └── utils.ts                        # Tailwind class mergers (clsx/tailwind-merge)
```

---

## 💻 Development Commands

In the project directory, you can run:

### Start Development Server
Starts the Next.js development server with Turbopack enabled on [http://localhost:3000](http://localhost:3000):
```bash
npm run dev
```

### Production Build Check
Compiles the application, runs TypeScript type-checking, and generates optimized static pages:
```bash
npm run build
```

### Run Production Server
Starts the built application in production mode:
```bash
npm run start
```

### Linting Check
Scans the project files for ESLint errors:
```bash
npm run lint
```

# Accurix Financial (Desktop GUI & Web Application)

An enterprise-grade, Philippine GAAP / IFRS-compliant **Double-Entry Accounting & Financial Ledger Suite** developed in Java 25 LTS, JDBC, and MySQL 8. Features both a **100% Native Desktop Java GUI** (FlatLaf with Vercel Geist Light aesthetic, Java2D vector icons, custom taskbar icon) and a responsive **Web Application** (Java Servlets 4.0, JSP, JSTL 1.2, Apache Tomcat).

Designed and structured according to Clean Architecture and MVC separation of concerns for a final computer science / information technology capstone project. All currency values are strictly formatted in **Philippine Pesos (₱)** with zero foreign currency symbols.

---

## 1. Dual Deployment Modes

The system provides two interchangeable user interfaces backed by the exact same MySQL database layer (`accounting_db`):

| Feature | 100% Desktop GUI Window | Web Browser Application |
|---|---|---|
| **Master Launcher** | `run.bat` (Option `[1]`) or `Accurix Financial.lnk` | `run.bat` (Option `[2]`) |
| **Concurrent Run** | `run.bat` (Option `[3]` launches BOTH GUI and Web concurrently) |
| **Technology** | Java Swing + FlatLaf 3.4.1 (Vercel Geist Light) | Java Servlets 4.0 + JSP 2.3 + JSTL 1.2 |
| **Design System** | Vercel Geist Light (100% Light Mode, monochrome) | Vercel Geist Light (100% Light Mode, monochrome) |
| **Iconography** | Java2D Vector Geometric Icons (Zero emojis) | Clean SVG Vector Icons (Zero emojis) |
| **Branding / Icon** | Multi-res `app_icon.ico` (Taskbar & Titlebar) | Multi-res `favicon.png` & `favicon.ico` |
| **Currency** | Strictly Philippine Pesos (`PHP ₱#,##0.00`) | Strictly Philippine Pesos (`PHP ₱#,##0.00`) |
| **Persistence** | Direct JDBC connection pool (`accounting_db`) | Direct JDBC connection pool (`accounting_db`) |
| **Platform** | Standalone Desktop Application Window | Web Browser (`http://localhost:8888/accounting`) |

---

## 2. Project Team & Module Ownership

| Name | Role | Module Responsibilities |
|---|---|---|
| **Aranez, Hannah Bea C.** | Project Manager | Project Schedule, Task Assignment, Weekly Progress & Final Compilation |
| **Baydal, Nica** | System Analyst | System Description, Objectives, Requirements, Use Case, DFD & Flowcharts |
| **Cabase, Wincel James A.** | Lead Dev (Journals & JDBC) | JDBC Connection Manager, Journal Form, Save/Edit Servlets & Live Validation |
| **Cortes, Ashlee Nicole B.** | Lead Presenter & Docs | Setup Guide, User Manual, Presentation Deck & Live Demo Script |
| **Gabutan, Ivan G.** | Security & Auth | Users Database, BCrypt 10-Round Hashing, Session Management & Settings |
| **Gimena, Byn Jumer L.** | Financial Reports Lead | Trial Balance, Income Statement, Balance Sheet, Date Filtering & Print Views |
| **Mamites, Angelique P.** | QA & Testing Lead | QA Test Plan, Automated JUnit Suites (22/22 Tests), Defect Tracking & Sign-Off |
| **Melgar, Ashley Rosse** | UI / Frontend Lead | Vercel Geist Light Layout, Sidebar, Cards, Buttons & Responsive CSS |
| **Pacaña, Kim Y.** | General Ledger Lead | Chronological Postings, Normal Balance Sign Logic & Running Calculations |
| **Villorejo, Joshua Niño A.** | Database Lead | Schema DDL, ERD, Primary/Foreign Keys, Constraints & Seed Data |

---

## 3. Core Features & Capabilities

- **Authentication & Security:**
  - Salted 10-round BCrypt password hashing (`jBCrypt`).
  - `AuthFilter` URL interception preventing unauthorized direct page access.
  - Session invalidation on sign-out with cache control to prevent browser history caching.
- **Double-Entry Engine:**
  - Strict mathematical equilibrium: $\sum \text{Debits} = \sum \text{Credits}$.
  - Real-time client-side calculation disables save button if an entry is unbalanced.
  - Server-side double validation intercepts forged or malformed requests.
  - Atomic database transactions with connection rollbacks ensuring zero corrupted entries.
- **General Ledger:**
  - Real-time ledger updates for every account.
  - Dynamic Normal Balance calculations:
    - **Asset / Expense:** $\text{Balance} = \text{Debits} - \text{Credits}$
    - **Liability / Equity / Revenue:** $\text{Balance} = \text{Credits} - \text{Debits}$
  - Historical carryovers: Pre-period transactions automatically summarize into a "Beginning Balance" row.
- **GAAP Financial Reporting:**
  - **Trial Balance:** Ending balances across all accounts verifying mathematical equality.
  - **Income Statement:** Real-time computation of operating revenue, expenses, and net profit.
  - **Balance Sheet:** Confirms $\text{Assets} = \text{Liabilities} + \text{Equity}$ with dynamic absorption of current net profit into Owner's Equity.
  - **Print-Friendly:** One-click `@media print` styling strips navigation and renders formal paper financial statements.
- **Chart of Accounts & Live Dashboard:**
  - Full CRUD for Chart of Accounts across 5 core types.
  - Real-time MySQL aggregation cards for Assets, Liabilities, Equity, and Net Income in Philippine Pesos (`₱`).
- **Vercel Geist Light Design:**
  - Monochrome palette: Pitch Black (`#000000`), Dark Charcoal (`#262626`), Crisp White (`#FFFFFF`), Light Border (`#EAEAEA`).
  - Sleek button hover interactions: Secondary buttons feature crisp `#000000` hover borders; Primary buttons feature subtle charcoal hover transitions.
  - High-DPI Java2D geometric vector icons (zero unicode emojis).
  - Custom multi-resolution application icon (`app_icon.ico`) with Windows taskbar dock integration.

---

## 4. Technology Stack

- **Backend:** Java 25 LTS, Java Servlets 4.0, JSTL 1.2
- **Desktop GUI:** Java Swing, FlatLaf 3.4.1 (Vercel Geist Light), Java2D Vector Graphics
- **Persistence:** JDBC, MySQL 8.0+ (InnoDB engine with foreign keys)
- **Security:** jBCrypt 0.4 (10 salt rounds)
- **Build & Packaging:** Apache Maven 3.9.6 (`accounting-system.war`)
- **Server:** Apache Tomcat 9.0+ / 10.1+ (via XAMPP Tomcat on port 8888)
- **Frontend:** HTML5, Modern Vanilla JavaScript, CSS3 (Vercel Geist Light tokens)
- **Testing:** JUnit 4.13.2 (23 unit tests passing, 100% pass rate)

---

## 5. Quick Start Guide (Unified Master Launcher)

The project includes a single master interactive launcher [`run.bat`](run.bat) at the root (and a pre-configured Windows desktop shortcut [`Accurix Financial.lnk`](Accurix%20Financial.lnk)).

```
======================================================================
            ACCURIX FINANCIAL -- DOUBLE-ENTRY LEDGER SUITE
                Philippine GAAP / IFRS Compliant [PHP]
======================================================================

  Select which system you would like to run:

  [1] Native Desktop Java GUI (Accurix Desktop Application)
  [2] Web-Based Application (Accurix Web on Apache Tomcat)
  [3] Launch BOTH Systems Concurrently (Desktop GUI + Web System)
  [4] Stop Web Application (Shut down Apache Tomcat server)
  [5] Exit
======================================================================
```

1. Ensure MySQL is running in your **XAMPP Control Panel** (port 3306).
2. Double-click [`run.bat`](run.bat) or [`Accurix Financial.lnk`](Accurix%20Financial.lnk).
3. Choose an option:
   - Press **`1`**: Launches the **100% Native Desktop Java GUI** window with high-DPI scaling, custom vector icons, and Windows taskbar branding.
   - Press **`2`**: Builds the WAR, synchronizes it to Tomcat, launches Apache Tomcat on port 8888, and opens your browser at `http://localhost:8888/accounting`.
   - Press **`3`**: Launches **BOTH** the Desktop GUI and the Web Application concurrently over the same database.
   - Press **`4`**: Stops Apache Tomcat and frees port 8888.
   - Press **`5`**: Exits the launcher.

> [!NOTE]
> Secondary standalone launch scripts are neatly organized in the [`scripts/`](scripts/) directory:
> - [`scripts/start-accounting-gui.bat`](scripts/start-accounting-gui.bat)
> - [`scripts/start-accounting-system.bat`](scripts/start-accounting-system.bat)
> - [`scripts/stop-accounting-system.bat`](scripts/stop-accounting-system.bat)

### Manual CLI Execution
```bash
# Run unit test suite (22 tests)
mvn test

# Launch Desktop GUI directly from terminal
mvn compile exec:java

# Build WAR package for Tomcat
mvn clean package
```

---

## 6. Default Demonstration Credentials

| Username | Password | Role | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `admin` | `admin123` | Administrator | Full administrative and ledger privileges |
| `accountant` | `password123` | Senior Accountant | Standard accounting and reporting access |
| `igabutan` | `password123` | Accountant | Ivan G. Gabutan's demonstration account |

---

## 7. Project Documentation Index

All project deliverables and defense guides are maintained in the [`docs/`](docs/) directory and project root:

- 📄 [**Project Development Specification (.docx)**](Accounting_System_Project_Development_Document.docx): Formal Word specification covering scope, team work plan, architecture, database design, 22 unit tests, and defect logs.
- 📖 [**Setup & User Guide**](docs/SETUP_AND_USER_GUIDE.md): Environment prerequisites, database configuration, deployment instructions, and module-by-module user manual.
- 📐 [**System Architecture & Diagrams**](docs/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE_DIAGRAMS.md): Mermaid Entity-Relationship Diagram (ERD), Use Case Diagram, Data Flow Diagrams (Level 0 & Level 1), System Flowchart, and Clean Architecture model.
- 🧪 [**Testing & QA Report**](docs/TESTING_AND_QA_REPORT.md): Quality assurance test strategy, 22 automated JUnit results, 28 manual integration scenarios, defect lifecycle log (BUG-001–008), and formal sign-offs.
- 🎤 [**Presentation Deck & Live Demo Script**](docs/DEMO_SCRIPT_AND_PRESENTATION.md): 11-slide presentation outline with speaker notes, timed live demo walkthrough, and anticipated instructor Q&A technical defense.

---

## 8. Automated Test Execution

To execute the automated regression test suite, run:
```bash
mvn test
```
**Results:** `Tests run: 22, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0` (100% Pass Rate).

# Beauty Hub E-Commerce

Beauty Hub is a PHP and MariaDB e-commerce application for selling beauty and makeup products. It includes a customer storefront, authentication, product browsing, search, cart and checkout, order history, profile management, and an administrator panel for products, inventory, orders, and users.

The project uses a small custom MVC-style architecture. Apache receives the request, `public/index.php` registers the routes and dispatches the request, a controller coordinates the operation, a model reads or writes MariaDB through PDO, and a view renders the result inside a shared layout.

## Quick Navigation

### Start Here: Application Bootstrap

| What you need to find | Exact file | What it contains |
| --- | --- | --- |
| First file executed from the project root | `index.php` | Includes the public front controller |
| Web front controller | `public/index.php` | Loads the application and registers every route |
| Pretty URL rewrite into `public/` | `.htaccess` | Sends non-public root requests to `public/` |
| Route rewrite into `public/index.php` | `public/.htaccess` | Sends non-file/non-directory URLs to the router |
| Route matching and controller dispatch | `app/core/Router.php` | Normalizes URLs, matches methods/paths, loads controllers, and renders 404 |
| Application constants and URL settings | `app/config/app.php` | `BASE_URL`, app name/version, currency, shipping, and upload paths |
| Database environment and defaults | `app/config/database.php` | Host, user, password, database name, and local/deployment selection |
| PDO connection and query helpers | `app/core/Database.php` | Shared PDO instance and fetch/execute methods |
| Base controller services | `app/core/Controller.php` | Model loading, views, JSON, redirects, authentication, and admin checks |
| Session and authentication state | `app/core/Session.php` | Login state, roles, flash messages, guest cart ID, and CSRF helpers |

### Storefront Page Lookup

| Page or feature | Route | Controller | View or supporting file |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Home page | `GET /` | `HomeController::index()` | `app/views/storefront/home/index.php` |
| About page | `GET /about` | `HomeController::about()` | `app/views/storefront/pages/about.php` |
| Contact page | `GET /contact` | `HomeController::contact()` | `app/views/storefront/pages/contact.php`, `public/assets/js/main.js` |
| Privacy page | `GET /privacy` | `HomeController::privacy()` | `app/views/storefront/pages/privacy.php` |
| Terms page | `GET /terms` | `HomeController::terms()` | `app/views/storefront/pages/terms.php` |
| Product catalog | `GET /products` | `ProductController::index()` | `app/views/storefront/products/catalog.php`, `Product.php` |
| Product detail | `GET /products/detail/{id}` where `{id}` accepts an ID or slug | `ProductController::detail()` | `app/views/storefront/products/detail.php`, `Product.php` |
| Search results | `GET /products/search` | `ProductController::search()` | `app/views/storefront/products/search.php`, `Product.php` |
| Flash sale | `GET /flash-sale` | `ProductController::flashSale()` | `app/views/storefront/deals/flash-sale.php` |
| New arrivals | `GET /new-arrivals` | `ProductController::newArrivals()` | `app/views/storefront/deals/new-arrivals.php` |
| Shopping cart page | `GET /cart` | `CartController::index()` | `app/views/storefront/cart/index.php`, `Cart.php` |
| Checkout page | `GET /checkout` | `CheckoutController::index()` | `app/views/storefront/cart/checkout.php` |
| Login | `GET|POST /login` | `AuthController::login()` | `app/views/storefront/auth/login.php`, `User.php` |
| Registration | `GET|POST /register` | `AuthController::register()` | `app/views/storefront/auth/register.php`, `User.php` |
| Logout | `GET /logout` | `AuthController::logout()` | `Session.php` and redirect response |
| Customer profile | `GET|POST /profile` | `ProfileController::index()` | `app/views/storefront/profile/index.php`, `User.php` |
| Customer order history | `GET /orders` | `OrderController::list()` | `app/views/storefront/orders/list.php`, `Order.php` |
| Customer order detail | `GET /orders/detail/{id}` | `OrderController::detail()` | `app/views/storefront/orders/detail.php`, `Order.php` |
| Unmatched URL page | Any unregistered route | `Router::dispatch()` | `app/views/storefront/pages/404.php` rendered without a layout |

### Customer APIs and Browser Scripts

| Operation | Route or file | Implementation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Add cart item | `POST /api/cart/add` | `CartController::add()` and `public/assets/js/modules/cart.js` |
| Change cart quantity | `POST /api/cart/update` | `CartController::update()` and `Cart::updateQuantity()` |
| Remove cart item | `POST /api/cart/remove` | `CartController::remove()` and `Cart::remove()` |
| Read cart count | `GET /api/cart/count` | `CartController::count()` JSON response |
| Submit checkout order | `POST /checkout/process` | `CheckoutController::process()` and `Order::create()` |
| Storefront-wide interactions | `public/assets/js/main.js` | Live search and upcoming-drop UI |
| Cart requests/count badge | `public/assets/js/modules/cart.js` | AJAX cart operations |
| User dropdown | `public/assets/js/modules/dropdown.js` | Header account-menu interaction |
| Toast notifications | `public/assets/js/modules/toast.js` | Shared browser toast behavior |

### Administrator Lookup

| Admin feature | Route | Controller | View or script |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard | `GET /admin` or `/admin/dashboard` | `Admin\\DashboardController::index()` | `app/views/admin/dashboard/index.php` |
| Product list | `GET /admin/products` | `Admin\\ProductAdminController::list()` | `app/views/admin/products/list.php` |
| Add product | `GET|POST /admin/products/add` | `ProductAdminController::add()` | `app/views/admin/products/add.php` |
| Edit product | `GET|POST /admin/products/edit/{id}` | `ProductAdminController::edit()` | `app/views/admin/products/edit.php` |
| Delete product | `GET /admin/products/delete/{id}` | `ProductAdminController::delete()` | Redirect response |
| Inventory | `GET /admin/inventory` | `Admin\\InventoryController::index()` | `app/views/admin/inventory/index.php` |
| Update stock | `POST /admin/inventory/updateStock` | `InventoryController::updateStock()` | Redirect to inventory |
| Barcode/SKU lookup | `GET /admin/api/barcode?code={barcodeOrSku}` | `InventoryController::barcodeApi()` | JSON response and `admin.js` |
| Order list | `GET /admin/orders` | `Admin\\OrderAdminController::list()` | `app/views/admin/orders/list.php` |

## Request Flow

A normal request follows this path:

1. Apache applies the root `.htaccess`, which rewrites requests into `public/`.
2. `public/.htaccess` serves existing files/directories directly and rewrites other URLs to `public/index.php?url=...`.
3. `public/index.php` loads configuration, core classes, models, starts the session, and registers routes.
4. `app/core/Router.php` normalizes the URL, matches the HTTP method and path in registration order, loads the controller, and calls its action.
5. The controller checks authentication when needed, asks a model for data, and chooses a view, JSON response, or redirect.
6. `app/core/Database.php` executes prepared PDO queries against MariaDB.
7. `app/core/Controller.php::view()` buffers the selected view and then loads `main.php`, `admin.php`, or no layout.

Example product-page trace:

```text
GET /products/detail/12 or /products/detail/velvet-lipstick
  -> public/index.php
  -> ProductController::detail($idOrSlug)
  -> Product::findById() or Product::findBySlug()
  -> app/views/storefront/products/detail.php
  -> app/views/layouts/main.php
  -> app/views/layouts/header.php and footer.php
```

The router's 404 fallback and product/order-not-found branches call the 404 view without a layout, so those responses do not include the normal header, footer, or layout stylesheet links.

### ERD relationship details

| Relationship | Database rule | Application meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `categories.id` -> `products.category_id` | Foreign key, delete cascades | A category groups its products |
| `products.id` -> `cart_items.product_id` | Foreign key, delete cascades | A cart row points to the product being purchased |
| `users.id` -> `cart_items.user_id` | Nullable foreign key, delete cascades | A cart can belong to a signed-in user; guest carts use `session_id` |
| `users.id` -> `orders.user_id` | Foreign key, delete cascades | Each order belongs to one customer |
| `orders.id` -> `order_items.order_id` | Foreign key, delete cascades | An order contains one or more saved line items |
| `products.id` -> `order_items.product_id` | No declared foreign key in current dump | The application stores the product ID while also snapshotting name and price |
| `upcoming_drops` | No foreign keys | Independent home-page release announcements |

`order_items` stores `product_name`, `price`, `quantity`, and `total_price` so an order retains the purchased line details even if the product later changes. The current database does not enforce that `product_id` still exists.

The SQL also defines unique keys for `users.email`, `categories.slug`, `products.slug`, `products.sku`, `products.barcode`, and `orders.order_number`. Additional non-unique indexes support `cart_items.product_id`, `cart_items.user_id`, `orders.user_id`, and `order_items.order_id`. All `order_items` columns are `NOT NULL`; several other tables use nullable fields with SQL defaults, as shown in the dump.

```mermaid
  Controllers --> Views[Storefront views and main layout]
  Controllers --> Response[Redirects or JSON]
  Views --> Browser
  Response --> Browser
  Browser --> Customer
  Browser -. AJAX/API requests .-> Apache
```

### Level-1 DFD: administrator flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  Admin[Administrator] --> AdminUI[Admin views and admin.js]
  AdminUI --> Apache[Apache and rewrite rules]
  Apache --> Router[Router]
  Router --> Controllers[Admin controllers]
  Controllers <--> Auth[requireAdmin and Session]
  Controllers --> Models[Product, Category, Order, and User models]
  Models <--> Database[(MariaDB tables)]
  Models --> Controllers
  Controllers --> AdminViews[Admin views and admin layout]
  Controllers --> AdminResponse[Redirects or JSON]
  AdminViews --> AdminUI
  AdminResponse --> AdminUI
  AdminUI --> Admin
  AdminUI -. AJAX/API requests .-> Apache
```

### DFD process responsibilities

| Process | Implemented by | Input | Output |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Route request | `public/index.php`, `app/core/Router.php` | HTTP method and URL | Controller action call or 404 page |
| Render storefront | Controllers, `Controller::view()`, `layouts/main.php` | Model data and view path | HTML page with header/footer |
| Manage session | `app/core/Session.php` | Login, logout, flash, guest activity | Session values and access decisions |
| Read catalog | `ProductController`, `Product.php`, `Category.php` | Category, search, sort, product ID/slug | Product/category records and JSON search results |
| Manage cart | `CartController`, `Cart.php` | Product ID, quantity, cart item ID | Cart rows, totals, count JSON |
| Place order | `CheckoutController`, `Order.php` | Authenticated user, shipping fields, cart rows | Order/order-item rows, stock updates, confirmation redirect |
| Manage admin data | Admin controllers and models | Admin forms and API requests | Updated products, stock, users, orders, and metrics |

The DFD intentionally groups individual model queries into one `Models` process for readability. The model query dependencies are: `User` -> `users` and joined `orders`; `Category` -> `categories` and joined `products`; `Product` -> `products`, `categories`, and `upcoming_drops`; `Cart` -> `cart_items` and joined `products`; and `Order` -> `orders`, `order_items`, joined `users`, and joined `products`. `ProfileController` also loads the signed-in user's orders through `Order`; these are not limited to a recent subset. The dashboard reads `Product::getLowStock()` in addition to product and user/order metrics. `upcoming_drops` is read by the home-page product flow and is independent of the other tables.

The current checkout flow writes directly to MariaDB through `Order::create()` and then clears the cart. There is no external payment, email, or notification process in the DFD because those integrations are not implemented.

## Frontend Architecture Diagram

Beauty Hub uses server-rendered PHP templates. It does not use React, Vue, Angular, or a client-side routing framework. A controller selects one view, `Controller::view()` captures that view as `$content`, and the selected layout places the content inside the complete HTML document. The browser then loads the linked CSS, JavaScript, images, logos, and videos.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Request[Browser request] --> Route[public/index.php and Router]
  Route --> StoreController[Storefront or customer controller]
  Route --> AdminController[Administrator controller]
  Route --> NotFound[404 view without layout]
  StoreController --> NotFound

  StoreController --> StoreView[Selected storefront view]
  StoreView --> MainLayout[layouts/main.php]
  MainLayout --> Header[layouts/header.php]
  MainLayout --> StoreContent[Rendered page content]
  MainLayout --> Footer[layouts/footer.php]
  MainLayout --> StoreScripts[toast.js, cart.js, dropdown.js, main.js]
  MainLayout --> StoreCSS[variables.css and style.css]

  AdminController --> AdminView[Selected admin view]
  AdminView --> AdminLayout[layouts/admin.php]
  AdminLayout --> Sidebar[layouts/admin-sidebar.php]
  AdminLayout --> AdminHeader[layouts/admin-header.php]
  AdminLayout --> AdminContent[Rendered admin content]
  AdminLayout --> AdminScripts[toast.js and admin.js]
  AdminLayout --> AdminCSS[variables.css, style.css, and admin.css]
  NotFound --> Browser[Direct 404 response]

  StoreScripts --> StoreAssets[Storefront interactions]
  AdminScripts --> AdminAssets[Admin interactions]
  StoreAssets -. AJAX/API requests .-> Route
  AdminAssets -. AJAX/API requests .-> Route
  StoreView --> StoreMedia[Storefront media assets]
  AdminView --> AdminMedia[Admin media assets]
  MainLayout --> SharedMedia[Shared logos and favicon]

  Header --> Browser
  StoreContent --> Browser
  Footer --> Browser
  Sidebar --> Browser
  AdminHeader --> Browser
  AdminContent --> Browser
  StoreAssets --> Browser
  AdminAssets --> Browser
  StoreCSS --> Browser
  AdminCSS --> Browser
  StoreMedia --> Browser
  AdminMedia --> Browser
  SharedMedia --> Browser
```

### Frontend branch details

| Branch | Layout composition | Shared resources | Page examples |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Storefront | `main.php` -> `header.php` + selected view content + `footer.php` | `variables.css`, `style.css`, `toast.js`, `cart.js`, `dropdown.js`, `main.js` | Home, catalog, product detail, cart, checkout, profile, orders |
| Administrator | `admin.php` -> `admin-sidebar.php` + `admin-header.php` + selected view content | `variables.css`, `style.css`, `admin.css`, `toast.js`, `admin.js` | Dashboard, products, inventory, orders, users |

### Frontend rendering responsibilities

- `app/views/layouts/main.php` creates the storefront HTML document, includes the global header/footer, prints `$content`, exposes `BASE_URL` and `CURRENCY` to JavaScript, and loads storefront scripts.
- `app/views/layouts/admin.php` creates the admin document, includes the sidebar/header, prints `$content`, shows admin flash messages, and loads admin scripts.
- `app/views/layouts/header.php` calculates the cart count, renders desktop/mobile navigation, global search, cart access, account controls, and the mobile navigation drawer.
- `app/views/components/` contains reusable markup, especially `product-card.php`, which is used by product grids and related-product sections.
- `public/assets/css/variables.css` defines shared design tokens; `style.css` styles the customer experience; `admin.css` styles the admin experience.
- `public/assets/js/` adds progressive browser interactions and AJAX behavior. Page navigation and primary data rendering still come from PHP routes and views. `admin.js` filtering applies only where the product-list `#adminTableSearch` element exists.
- `app/views/components/top-bar.php` exists but is not included by either layout or the current page views.
- The 404 fallback bypasses both layouts, so it is not part of the normal frontend composition shown above.

## Configuration and Local Setup

### Requirements

- XAMPP with Apache and MariaDB/MySQL
- PHP with PDO MySQL enabled
- Apache `mod_rewrite` enabled
- A browser

No Composer or Node package installation is required by the current source tree.

### Installation

1. Place the project in `C:\xampp\htdocs\marsha` or another Apache document-root folder.
2. Start Apache and MySQL from the XAMPP Control Panel.
3. Open phpMyAdmin at `http://localhost/phpmyadmin`.
4. Import `beautyhub_db.sql`. The file creates `beautyhub_db` and selects it automatically.
5. Visit `http://localhost/marsha/` in a browser.
6. For product and avatar uploads, ensure `public/assets/img/products/` and `public/assets/img/avatars/` are writable by the web server.

Local database defaults are defined in `app/config/database.php`:

```text
Host: localhost
User: root
Password: empty by default
Database: beautyhub_db
Charset: utf8mb4
```

For deployment, set `DB_HOST`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASS`, and `DB_NAME` as environment variables instead of relying on source-code defaults. Although environment variables take precedence, `app/config/database.php` currently contains a hardcoded InfinityFree fallback credential. Remove and rotate that credential before publishing or deploying the repository. `app/config/app.php` also defines `BASE_URL`, currency, shipping thresholds, and upload paths.

## Frontend Assets

- `public/assets/css/variables.css`: colors, typography, spacing, radii, shadows, and transitions.
- `public/assets/css/style.css`: storefront layout, catalog, cards, cart, checkout, and responsive styles.
- `public/assets/css/admin.css`: dashboard, admin navigation, tables, forms, and inventory styles.
- `public/assets/js/main.js`: general storefront behavior, live search, and upcoming-drop notifications. The `Notify Me` action only disables the button and shows a toast; it does not save a subscription or send email.
- `public/assets/js/modules/cart.js`: cart API calls and cart-count updates.
- `public/assets/js/modules/dropdown.js`: account/user dropdown behavior.
- `public/assets/js/modules/toast.js`: toast notifications.
- `public/assets/js/admin.js`: admin filtering and barcode lookup.
- `public/assets/img/products/`: product and category imagery. Product administration uploads files into this directory.
- `public/assets/img/avatars/`: default and user avatar images.
- `public/assets/img/logo/`: logo and favicon files.
- `public/assets/video/`: home-page hero video files.

The shared header and navigation are in `app/views/layouts/header.php`. The shared footer is in `app/views/layouts/footer.php`. The storefront shell is `app/views/layouts/main.php`; the admin shell is `app/views/layouts/admin.php`.

## Important Maintenance Notes

These points describe current behavior that a maintainer or reviewer should know:

- `public/index.php` currently registers the order-status POST route twice. The router checks the first `orderStatusUpdate` handler, finds no such method, then reaches the effective `updateStatus` registration; the dead alias should be removed.
- CSRF helper methods exist in `app/core/Session.php`, but no rendered form currently includes a token and no mutating controller or endpoint verifies one.
- Product deletion and logout currently use GET routes even though they change application state.
- Cart quantity validation should also enforce the total quantity already in the cart, not only the quantity in a new add request.
- Order creation performs multiple database changes and should ideally use a transaction with final stock validation.
- Product uploads in `Admin\\ProductAdminController.php` currently have no server-side file type, MIME, size, or upload-result validation. Profile avatar uploads in `ProfileController.php` use an extension allowlist and upload error check, but do not validate MIME type or size.
- Do not commit production database credentials. Environment variables are supported, but the current InfinityFree fallback in `app/config/database.php` must be removed and rotated.
- Cart merging moves guest rows to the user ID but does not consolidate duplicate product rows.
- `Order::create()` inserts the order, inserts order items, and decrements stock without a database transaction or final stock revalidation.
- Checkout labels support GCash/Maya, card, and cash on delivery only as stored order fields. There is no payment gateway, QR flow, card processor, or payment verification.
- Orders are initially created with pending payment and fulfillment statuses; administrators change status through `OrderAdminController::updateStatus()`.
- The login view exposes seeded demo credentials for customer and administrator testing. Treat those accounts as development-only and change or remove them outside local testing.
- Storefront pages use Boxicons and some inline SVG markup, plus remote Google Fonts, Unsplash fallbacks, and UI Avatars. Offline rendering and strict content-security policies may therefore differ.
- The mobile header search submits `search`, while `ProductController::index()` reads `q`; mobile catalog filtering through that search field is currently inconsistent.

## How to Trace a Feature During a Presentation

Use this order when asked where a feature is implemented:

1. Find its URL in `public/index.php`.
2. Open the controller action named by that route in `app/controllers/` or `app/controllers/Admin/`.
3. Follow the model method used by the controller in `app/models/`.
4. Follow the view path passed to `view()` in `app/views/`.
5. For reusable appearance, inspect `app/views/components/` and `public/assets/css/`.
6. For browser-side interaction or AJAX, inspect `public/assets/js/`.
7. For stored data, inspect the matching table in `beautyhub_db.sql`.

For example, to trace the product section:

```text
Route: public/index.php -> GET products
Controller: app/controllers/ProductController.php -> index()
Model: app/models/Product.php -> getAll()
Page: app/views/storefront/products/catalog.php
Reusable tile: app/views/components/product-card.php
Styles: public/assets/css/style.css
Data: beautyhub_db.sql -> products and categories
```

LinkedIn Easy Apply automation tool built with Playwright that logs in, discovers jobs, auto-fills application forms with profile data and AI-assisted answers, tracks runtime state, and generates session reports.

## Requirements

- Python 3.11+
- Windows PowerShell (recommended for bootstrap scripts)

## Project Layout

```text
src/
  app.py                      # Main orchestration flow
  config.py                   # Loads config/data.json
  logging_setup.py            # Shared Rich logging + console
  models.py                   # SessionStats and JobRecord
  __main__.py                 # python -m src entrypoint
  automation/
    easy_apply_agent.py
    answering_mixin.py
    form_interaction_mixin.py
    modal_submit_mixin.py
  services/
    ai.py
    linkedin.py
    reporting.py
  storage/
    json_store.py
  ui/
    dashboard.py

config/
  data.json                   # Candidate/job preferences (local private data)

assets/
  dummy.pdf                   # Local sample resume (replace with your own)

runtime/
  application_history.json    # Runtime state
  daily_stats.json            # Runtime state
  job_queue.json              # Runtime state
  linkedin_state.json         # Runtime state
  session_report.html         # Generated report output

scripts/
  start.ps1                   # Bootstrap .venv, install deps if needed, run app
  start.cmd                   # cmd wrapper for start.ps1

main.py                       # Root launcher (calls src.app.run)
requirements.txt              # Python dependencies
pyproject.toml                # Packaging metadata
tests/                        # Unit tests
```

## Quick Start (Recommended)

1. Create local config files from the samples:

```powershell
Copy-Item .env.example .env
Copy-Item config/data.sample.json config/data.json
```

Then edit your local `.env` and `config/data.json` with your real values.

2. Run bootstrap script (creates `.venv`, installs requirements if changed, then runs app):

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/start.ps1
```

From cmd:

```bat
scripts\start.cmd
```

## Setup Only (No Launch)

Use this when you only want environment + dependency setup:

```powershell
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/start.ps1 -NoRun
```

## Manual Run Options

Run with root launcher:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe main.py
```

Run as module:

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m src
```

Optional console script (after editable install):

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m pip install -e .
linkedin-autopilot
```

## Tests

```powershell
.\.venv\Scripts\python.exe -m unittest discover -s tests -p "test_*.py"
```

## Configuration

- Set `application_settings.resume_path` to your resume file path (for example `assets/your_resume.pdf`).
- Runtime/session files are stored in `runtime/`.

## Run

- Windows quick start: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/start.ps1`
- Manual run: `python main.py`
- Module run: `python -m src`

readme:
# Facebook Page & Bot API Service (TypeScript)

A production-ready, modular Node.js + Express + TypeScript service built according to Meta's official **Facebook Pages API** and **Messenger API** specifications.

---

## Features

- **Nimji AI Assistant**: Built-in intelligent conversational assistant powered by Google Gemini web scraper with rolling multi-turn memory.
- **Page Info & Settings**: Retrieve Page details, cover photos, follower counts, and settings.
- **Feed Posting**: Publish posts, link updates, media, and scheduled posts to Page feeds.
- **Comment Management**: Read, reply to, and delete comments on Page posts.
- **Analytics & Insights**: Fetch metrics like `page_views_total`, `page_follows`, and post engagements.
- **Mentions & Tagged Content**: Track posts tagging or mentioning your Page.
- **Meta Webhooks**: Handle GET challenge verification and HMAC SHA-256 (`x-hub-signature-256`) payload validation for real-time `feed` and `messages` updates.
- **Automated Bot Service**: Automatic replies to incoming Messenger messages, persistent menu postbacks, and Page comments with an extensible command registry.

---

## 🤖 Bot Commands in Messenger

Users chatting with your Facebook Page can use the following commands:

- **`nimji <question>`** *(or `/ai <question>`)* — Ask Nimji, the intelligent AI assistant powered by Google Gemini.
- **`nimji reset`** — Clears rolling conversation memory.
- **`help`** — Shows available bot commands.
- **`info`** — Shows live Facebook Page details (followers, category, about).
- **`hours`** — Shows operational hours.
- **`support`** — Provides customer support contact information.
- **`post <text>`** — *(Admin only)* Publishes a post to the Page feed directly from Messenger.

> **Smart AI Fallback:** Any freeform question or message sent to the Page that does not match an administrative command is automatically answered by Nimji AI!

---

## 🛠️ Step-by-Step Meta Developer Registration & Token Setup

Follow these official steps to register as a developer, obtain tokens, and configure Webhooks:

### Step 1: Register as a Meta Developer
1. Go to [Meta for Developers](https://developers.facebook.com/).
2. Log in with your Facebook account and click **Get Started** or **Register**.
3. Accept the Meta Platform Terms and complete developer verification.

### Step 2: Create a Meta App
1. Go to **[My Apps](https://developers.facebook.com/apps)** and click **Create App**.
2. Select **Other** > **Business** app type (or **Business / Page Management** use case).
3. Enter your App Name and contact email, then click **Create App**.

### Step 3: Add Facebook Pages API & Messenger Products
1. In your App Dashboard, navigate to **Add Products**.
2. Add **Facebook Pages API** and **Messenger**.

### Step 4: Generate a Page Access Token
1. Go to **[Graph API Explorer](https://developers.facebook.com/tools/explorer/)**.
2. In the top-right **Meta App** dropdown, select your newly created App.
3. In User/Page dropdown, select **Get Page Access Token**.
4. Grant the following required permissions:
   - `pages_show_list`
   - `pages_read_engagement`
   - `pages_manage_posts`
   - `pages_manage_engagement`
   - `pages_messaging`
   - `pages_manage_metadata`
5. Click **Generate Access Token** and grant access to your Facebook Page.
6. Copy the generated **Page Access Token** and **Page ID**.

> **Note (Token Longevity):** Short-lived tokens generated in Explorer expire in 1-2 hours. To generate a long-lived Page token, exchange it via:
> ```bash
> GET https://graph.facebook.com/v26.0/oauth/access_token?grant_type=fb_exchange_token&client_id={APP_ID}&client_secret={APP_SECRET}&fb_exchange_token={SHORT_LIVED_TOKEN}
> ```

### Step 5: Configure Webhooks
1. In your App Dashboard, select **Webhooks** > **Page**.
2. Set Callback URL to your public URL (e.g. `https://your-service.onrender.com/webhook`).
3. Set Verify Token to match `FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN` in your `.env` / Render environment.
4. Subscribe to `feed` and `messages` fields.

---

## 🚀 Environment Configuration

Copy `.env.example` to `.env` and fill in your credentials:

```env
PORT=3000
NODE_ENV=development

FACEBOOK_GRAPH_VERSION=v26.0
FACEBOOK_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN=your_page_access_token
FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET=your_facebook_app_secret
FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN=your_custom_webhook_verify_token
FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID=your_page_id

# Optional: Admin PSIDs allowed to execute /post in Messenger
FACEBOOK_ADMIN_PSIDS=

# Nimji AI (Google Gemini Web Chat Scraper)
COOKIES=your_gemini_browser_cookies_here
AT_TOKEN=your_at_token_here
F_SID=your_f_sid_here
BL_PARAM=boq_gemini-web-uiserver_20261014.09_p0
```

---

## 🏃 Running Locally

### Install Dependencies
```bash
npm install
```

### Type Checking
```bash
npm run typecheck
```

### Development Mode (with hot-reload)
```bash
npm run dev
```

### Production Build & Start
```bash
npm run build
npm start
```

---

## ☁️ Deploying to Render

This repository includes a `render.yaml` Blueprint file for automatic configuration on [Render](https://render.com).

### Render Web Service Settings:
- **Build Command**: `npm install && npm run build`
- **Start Command**: `npm start`
- **Health Check Path**: `/health`

### Environment Variables on Render:
Set the following under **Environment** in your Render service dashboard:
- `NODE_ENV`: `production`
- `FACEBOOK_GRAPH_VERSION`: `v26.0`
- `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ACCESS_TOKEN`: *(Your Page Access Token)*
- `FACEBOOK_APP_SECRET`: *(Your Meta App Secret)*
- `FACEBOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`: *(Your custom webhook verify token)*
- `FACEBOOK_PAGE_ID`: *(Your Page ID)*
- `FACEBOOK_ADMIN_PSIDS`: *(Optional comma-separated admin PSIDs)*
- `COOKIES`: *(Your Gemini browser cookies)*
- `AT_TOKEN`: *(Your Gemini AT token)*
- `F_SID`: *(Your Gemini F.SID)*
- `BL_PARAM`: `boq_gemini-web-uiserver_20261014.09_p0`

---

## 📡 API Endpoints Reference

### 1. Webhooks
- `GET /webhook` - Verification challenge endpoint (used by Meta App Dashboard).
- `POST /webhook` - Receives real-time updates (Feed posts, comments, Messenger messages). Protected by HMAC `x-hub-signature-256`.

### 2. Page Operations (`/api/page`)
- `GET /api/page/info` - Get basic information about the Page.
- `GET /api/page/settings` - Retrieve Page cover, about, and description settings.

- **🗣️ Custom Tokenizer**: Includes a dedicated Byte-Level BPE tokenizer trained heavily on domain data (Vocab: 441), offering 100x efficiency over generic tokenizers.

# NotebookLM Watermark Remover

A fast, lightweight, and pure Python CLI tool designed to cleanly detect and remove "NotebookLM" watermarks from **PDF documents**, **PowerPoint presentations (PPTX)**, and **images (PNG, JPG, WEBP)**. Instead of crudely placing solid blocks or blurring areas, it uses a hybrid approach: **PyMuPDF vector layer redaction**, **multi-scale template matching**, and **texture-preserving background patch healing** (with Telea inpainting fallback). --- ## Key Features - **Pure CLI Experience**: Lightweight Python script execution with zero heavy build tools, GUI overhead, or packaging bloat. - **Smart PDF Redaction**: Selectively removes the watermark from the PDF vector text layer, keeping background vector art intact while inpainting watermark icons. - **PowerPoint (PPTX) Support**: Automatically scans, cleans, and updates embedded slide images inside PPTX archives while maintaining layout and image compression. - **Image Cleaning**: Restores PNGs (including alpha/transparency channels), JPEGs, and WEBPs with sub-pixel resolution upscaling. - **Texture-Preserving Patch Healing**: Samples neighboring clean background regions to preserve grain, gradients, and paper textures. - **Batch Processing**: Clean entire folders containing mixed document and image formats in a single command. - **Preview Mode**: Fast preview on page 1 of PDFs before committing to large multi-page jobs. --- ## Installation ### 1. Clone the Repository ```bash git clone https://github.com/0xp47/notebooklm-watermark-remover.git cd notebooklm-watermark-remover ``` ### 2. Install Dependencies ```bash pip install -r requirements.txt ``` *(Optional)* Install locally as a system-wide command: ```bash pip install -e . ``` --- ## Quick Start & CLI Usage Run directly via the root `remove.py` script: ### Single File Cleaning ```bash # Clean a PDF document python remove.py document.pdf # Clean a PowerPoint slide deck python remove.py presentation.pptx # Clean an image (PNG with transparency, JPG, WEBP) python remove.py slide.png ``` *Cleaned files are saved automatically in the same directory with `_cleaned` suffix (e.g., `document_cleaned.pdf`).* ### Custom Output Destination ```bash python remove.py document.pdf -o path/to/cleaned_output.pdf ``` ### Batch Process a Folder ```bash # Clean all supported files in a folder python remove.py ./my_documents/ # Clean and output all results to a specific directory python remove.py ./my_documents/ -o ./cleaned_documents/ ``` ### Preview First Page (PDF Only) ```bash python remove.py document.pdf --preview ``` --- ## CLI Options & Tuning ``` usage: notebooklm-remover [-h] [-o OUTPUT] [--preview] [--margin-x MARGIN_X] [--margin-y MARGIN_Y] [--threshold THRESHOLD] [--text-threshold TEXT_THRESHOLD] [--scale SCALE] [--radius RADIUS] [--no-patch-heal] [--debug] [-v] path ``` | Flag | Type | Default | Description | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `path` | `str` | *Required* | Path to an input file (`.pdf`, `.pptx`, `.png`, `.jpg`, `.jpeg`, `.webp`) or folder. | | `-o, --output` | `str` | `None` | Custom output file or directory path (defaults to `_cleaned.`). | | `--preview` | `flag` | `False` | Process only the first page (PDF only). | | `--margin-x` | `int` | `400` | Search margin width from right edge (pixels/points). | | `--margin-y` | `int` | `120` | Search margin height from bottom edge (pixels/points). | | `--threshold` | `int` | `22` | Contrast difference threshold for candidate stroke extraction (0–255). | | `--text-threshold` | `float` | `0.45` | Template match correlation threshold for "NotebookLM" text detection. | | `--scale` | `float` | `3.5` | Upscaling render factor for high-resolution sub-pixel mask alignment. | | `--radius` | `int` | `3` | Inpaint radius for OpenCV Telea fallback. | | `--no-patch-heal` | `flag` | `False` | Disable texture patch healing and use standard inpainting directly. | | `--debug` | `flag` | `False` | Output intermediate detection masks and ROIs to `debug_watermark/`. | | `-v, --version` | `flag` | — | Display version number (`1.0.0`) and exit. | --- ## How It Works ``` ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Input File │ └──────────────┬────────────────┘ │ ┌──────────────────────┼──────────────────────┐ ▼ ▼ ▼ [ PDF Document ] [ PPTX Archive ] [ Image File ] │ │ │ Vector Redaction Unpack Media Upscale ROI │ │ │ └──────────────┬───────┴──────────────────────┘ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Watermark Detection ROI │ │ • Polarity check (L/D) │ │ • Multi-scale template │ │ • Connected component fusion│ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Reconstruction Core │ │ • Texture donor patch match │ │ • Alpha gradient blending │ │ • Telea inpaint fallback │ └───────────────┬───────────────┘ ▼ ┌───────────────────────────────┐ │ Cleaned Output Saved │ └───────────────────────────────┘ ``` --- ## readme:
# Unified API Server

FastAPI server with auto-loading service architecture. Drop a folder into `services/` — zero configuration required.

## Services

| Service | Endpoint | Description |
|---------|----------|-------------|
| **TTS** | `POST /tts` | Text-to-speech via Microsoft Edge Neural TTS |
| **Download** | `POST /unidl` | Video/audio download via yt-dlp |
| **QR Code** | `POST /qr` | QR code generation (PNG/SVG/PDF/EPS/TXT) via segno |

## Quick Start

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt
python main.py
```

Server starts at `http://localhost:8000`. Override with `API_PORT=3000 python main.py`.

## Usage

### TTS — `POST /tts`

Generate audio:
```json
{"text": "Hello world", "voice": "en-US-JennyNeural", "rate": "+0%", "pitch": "+0Hz"}
```

List all available voices:
```json
{"list_voices": true}
```

### Download — `POST /unidl`

```json
{"url": "https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dQw4w9WgXcQ", "quality": "720p"}
```

Returns the file directly with auto-cleanup.

### QR Code — `POST /qr`

Standard QR:
```json
{"data": "https://example.com", "format": "png"}
```

WiFi QR:
```json
{"ssid": "MyNetwork", "password": "secret123", "security": "WPA"}
```

## Project Structure

```
├── main.py              # Entry point
├── config.py            # Server settings (host, port, debug)
├── utils.py             # Shared utilities (internet check)
├── cache/               # All service runtime data
│   ├── tts/             # TTS audio cache
│   └── yt_dlp/          # Download temp files
├── services/
│   ├── __init__.py      # Auto-loader (ServiceLoader)
│   ├── edge_tts/        # TTS service
│   │   ├── config.py    # TTS settings
│   │   ├── models.py    # Request models
│   │   ├── engine.py    # Generation engine
│   │   ├── cache.py     # Audio cache
│   │   └── endpoints.py # API route
│   ├── yt_dlp/          # Download service
│   │   ├── config.py    # Download settings
│   │   ├── models.py    # Request models
│   │   ├── utils.py     # FFmpeg check, URL validation
│   │   ├── dependencies.py # FFmpeg auto-download
│   │   ├── downloader.py   # Download engine with retry
│   │   ├── config_builder.py # yt-dlp options builder
│   │   ├── formats.py   # Quality presets
│   │   └── endpoints.py # API route
│   └── qr/              # QR service
│       ├── models.py    # Request models
│       ├── generator.py # QR engine
│       └── endpoints.py # API route
└── tests/               # pytest suite
```

## Adding a Service

Create `services/myservice/endpoints.py`:

```python
from fastapi import APIRouter

router = APIRouter(prefix="/myservice", tags=["MyService"])

@router.get("/hello")
async def hello():
    return {"message": "Hello!"}
```

Restart the server. Done.

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `API_HOST` | `0.0.0.0` | Server host |
| `API_PORT` | `8000` | Server port |
| `API_DEBUG` | `false` | Debug mode (auto-reload) |
| `TTS_CACHE_ENABLED` | `true` | Enable TTS audio caching |
| `TTS_DEFAULT_VOICE` | `en-US-AnaNeural` | Default TTS voice |
| `TTS_MAX_TEXT_LENGTH` | `5000` | Max text length for TTS |
| `YTDLP_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` | `3` | Download retry attempts |
| `YTDLP_SOCKET_TIMEOUT` | `30` | Download socket timeout (s) |

## Testing

```bash
pytest
```

readme:
# Windows User Profile Renamer 🛠️

This repository provides a safe, step-by-step PowerShell-automated solution to rename a Windows user profile directory and its associated user account.

---

## The Problem
When you rename a Windows user account via the Control Panel or Settings, Windows renames the *display name* and the *login name*, but **it does not rename the user's profile folder** (e.g., `C:\Users\oldname` remains unchanged). 

Manually renaming this directory is highly risky because:
1. The folder is locked by active system processes while you are logged in.
2. Direct renaming breaks registry mappings, causing Windows to load a temporary profile instead.
3. Hardcoded paths inside applications (app data, settings) will break.

## The Solution
This toolkit automates the renaming process cleanly. It is composed of three scripts and a main control panel:
* **[control_panel.bat](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/control_panel.bat)**: The unified command-line control panel to manage the entire workflow.
* **[create_temp_admin.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/create_temp_admin.ps1)**: Provisions a temporary administrator account.
* **[rename_profile.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/rename_profile.ps1)**: Performs the profile directory rename, registry path update, and creates a directory junction for backward compatibility.
* **[remove_temp_admin.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/remove_temp_admin.ps1)**: Cleans up the temporary administrator account when finished.


---

## 📋 Prerequisites & Warnings

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Files Shared Location**: Because you must log out of your current account and log into the `temp` account, the scripts **must** be stored in a shared directory that both accounts can access. 
> 
> Please copy/move the entire toolkit folder to:
> `C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer`
> *(The toolkit has already been automatically prepared in this directory for you!)*

> [!WARNING]
> Renaming user profile directories modifies registry keys and system paths. **Ensure you back up any critical files before running the script.**

* **PowerShell Execution Policy**: You must allow running scripts. You can enable this temporarily by running:
  ```powershell
  Set-ExecutionPolicy -Scope Process -ExecutionPolicy Bypass
  ```
* **Administrator Privileges**: All scripts must be run as Administrator (the `control_panel.bat` script automatically requests admin privilege elevation).

---

## 🚀 Step-by-Step Guide

### Step 0: Clone the Repository and Copy to Public Directory (Crucial Setup)
Because Windows will sign you out of your current account to rename it, the scripts **must** be placed in a public directory that both your current account and the new temporary account can access.

1. Open PowerShell and clone the repository:
   ```powershell
   git clone https://github.com/0xp47/windows-user-profile-renamer.git
   ```
2. Copy the cloned folder into the Public folder:
   ```powershell
   Copy-Item -Path .\windows-user-profile-renamer -Destination C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer -Recurse -Force
   ```
   *(Or manually copy the folder and paste it into `C:\Users\Public\` so that the path becomes `C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer`)*


---

### Step 1: Create the Temporary Administrator Account
1. Open the shared folder: `C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer`
2. Double-click **[control_panel.bat](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/control_panel.bat)**.
3. Select Option `1` (Create Temporary Admin).
4. This creates a temporary user named `temp` with the password `123456` and grants it administrative privileges.


---

### Step 2: Switch to the Temporary Account
1. Save your work and **Sign Out** of your current account (`0x3EF8`).
2. On the Windows sign-in screen, select the **temp** account.
3. Log in using the password: `123456`.
4. Wait for Windows to finish setting up the temporary desktop (this takes about a minute).

---

### Step 3: Run the Renamer Script
1. Once logged into the `temp` account, open File Explorer and go to:
   `C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer`
2. Run **[control_panel.bat](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/control_panel.bat)**.
3. Select Option `2` (Run Profile Renamer).

#### What the script does:
* **Account Rename**: Renames the local user account from `0x3EF8` to `0xp47`.
* **Profile Folder Rename**: Renames `C:\Users\0x3EF8` to `C:\Users\0xp47`.
* **Registry Update**: Locates the Security Identifier (SID) of the account and updates the profile registry key path (`ProfileImagePath`) in `HKLM:\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList`.
* **Junction Creation**: Creates a directory junction pointing `C:\Users\0x3EF8` to `C:\Users\0xp47`. This is critical: if any legacy applications have hardcoded paths to your old profile name, they will resolve seamlessly to the new location.

---

### Step 4: Log back in and Clean up
1. **Sign Out** of the `temp` account.
2. Sign in to your newly renamed account: **0xp47**.
3. Open the shared folder: `C:\Users\Public\windows-user-profile-renamer`
4. Run **[control_panel.bat](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/control_panel.bat)**.
5. Select Option `3` (Remove Temporary Admin).
   * This safely deletes the `temp` user account and completely removes its temporary profile directory and associated registry values.

## 🛠️ Script Customization
If you need to rename a different user account, open **[rename_profile.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/rename_profile.ps1)** and edit the following values at the top of the file:

```powershell
$oldName = "0x3EF8"  # The current username
$newName = "0xp47"   # The desired username
```

---

## 📁 Repository Structure
* **[control_panel.bat](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/control_panel.bat)**: Main interactive Control Panel CLI launcher.
* **scripts/**: Subfolder containing core PowerShell scripts.
  * **[rename_profile.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/rename_profile.ps1)**: Main renamer utility.
  * **[create_temp_admin.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/create_temp_admin.ps1)**: Tool to set up the temporary profile `temp` with password `123456`.
  * **[remove_temp_admin.ps1](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/scripts/remove_temp_admin.ps1)**: Script to remove the temporary admin and clean up folders.
* **[README.md](file:///C:/Users/Public/windows-user-profile-renamer/README.md)**: Documentation and step-by-step instructions.

# XAMPP Repair Engine

An automated PowerShell-backed CLI utility designed to diagnose, isolate, and repair corrupted XAMPP MySQL/Apache installations on Windows. It fixes common startup crashes, resolves port conflicts, and optimizes database performance safely.

---

## 📖 Complete Documentation

A comprehensive guide explaining the internal mechanics, port resolution, system restoration, and recovery modes can be found in the [XAMPP Repair Guide](XAMPP_Repair_Guide.md).

---

## 🚀 Features

*   **Quick Repair Protocol:** Instantly purges locked `.pid` files, corrupt `aria_log_control` files, and mismatched `ib_logfile*` logs to clear process hangs.
*   **Advanced System Recovery (Smart Rebuild):** 
    *   **Port Conflict Scan & Kill:** Scans ports 80, 443, and 3306, automatically killing conflicting process threads (Skype, VMware, orphaned processes).
    *   **Tablespace Transplantation:** Replaces corrupted system databases (`mysql`, `performance_schema`, `phpmyadmin`) from XAMPP templates while preserving your main `ibdata1` shared tablespace.
    *   **Progressive Safe Boot:** If rebuild fails, injects `innodb_force_recovery` modes (1 to 3) to launch MySQL in Read-Only mode so you can export databases via phpMyAdmin.
*   **Table Optimization:** Runs `mysqlcheck` automatically to repair, defragment, and optimize all active schemas.
*   **Data Preservation & Factory Reset:** Create manual snapshots of the data folder at any time or execute a fresh factory reset state when files are unsalvageable.

## 🛠️ Menu Selection Overview

1.  **Quick Repair Protocol (Cache/Lock Purge):** Wipes locks and temporary logs. Databases are left untouched.
2.  **Advanced System Recovery (Deep Clean + Rebuild):** Rebuilds system databases and imports user schemas. *Note: Resets root password to blank (no password).*
3.  **Optimize Database Tables (Defrag/Repair):** Runs database checks and table optimizations.
4.  **Data Preservation (Manual Snapshot):** Safely backs up the `mysql/data` folder to a timestamped folder.
5.  **Heuristic Log Analysis (Error Stream):** Displays colored log outputs from `mysql_error.log`.
6.  **EMERGENCY FACTORY RESET:** Performs a clean restore from default XAMPP backups. Wipes current databases (creates quarantine first).
7.  **Terminate Session:** Safely exits the session.

## ⚠️ Requirements & Execution

1.  **Place the Script:** Place `Repair-Tool BETA.bat` in your project folder (expects default XAMPP at `C:\xampp`).
2.  **Run as Administrator:** Right-click `Repair-Tool BETA.bat` and select **Run as Administrator** (required for process isolation and stopping service threads).
